utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Thursday, 26th of November, 2009. Good morning to the four accused. Apparently two are ill. Good morning to the Defence counsel. Good morning, Witness. Good morning, Mr. Bos, Mr. Scott, and Madam Case Manager, and all the people assisting us. And I also greet the security officers present in the courtroom. We are to continue with cross-examination. It seems that the Prosecutor still has 40 minutes to complete his cross-examination. But before I ask him to proceed, I have a follow-up question for you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who was the commander of the operative zone of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll put my question again. Could you tell me, Witness, who was the commander of the operative zone of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat? I was without interpretation again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope the interpreters are awake now. I'll repeat my question for a third time. Can you tell me who was the commander of the operative zone of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We belonged to the Zone of Operations South-East, and the commander was Mica Lasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. When there were large-scale operations, were there joint operations conducted by several operative zones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, as far as we from Konjic are concerned, the answer is no. Only when we requested help, we simultaneously requested it from both zones of operations because that was our position between two or, if you will, three zones of operation, if we consider Central Bosnia too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were in your brigade on the 15th of April, 1993 -- this may be a difficult question, because I'm going to ask you whether you remember exactly what you were doing on the 15th of April. I couldn't answer such a question, personally, but you're younger than me, so it may be that your memory works better than mine. On the 15th of April, 1993, did you, by any chance, hear that the commander of the HVO brigade in Zenica, Zivko Totic, had been kidnapped by Muslims? Did you, by any chance, hear about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that you didn't know that then. When did you learn about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until our departure, that is, until our part of the brigade left the circle in which it was, a significant amount of time elapsed. But a number of people were kidnapped or detained, so I'm not really sure. I may have heard such accounts, but I didn't pay much attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're not aware of it. The reason why I'm asking this question is as follows. I'm very clear, transparent, in my questions. My questions are never tricky, there's never any trap. So the Prosecution says that there was an ultimatum on the 15th of April, and following the ultimatum there was an all-out HVO offensive in several municipalities, including in Central Bosnia; hence the attacks on Ahmici, Vitez, et cetera. One of the Defence cases in the Kordic or Blaskic cases was that the attacks on the 16th of April were only the result of this Totic gentleman being kidnapped, and as a result of that Colonel Blaskic, at 6.30 p.m. on the 15th of April, gave an order to mobilise the brigades for defensive actions. And that's the reason why I was asking you whether you'd heard that something had happened on the 15th of April. And you answered, No, so I must conclude from that that at the level of your brigade, on the 16th of April, there was no plan for defensive or offensive actions at your level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as we're concerned, in my brigade -- actually, parts of my brigade, that is, the 1st Battalion, we were attacked by the ABiH as soon as the 14th of April, and on the 16th, there were attacks of the ABiH in the area of my battalion, which was deployed at Konjic, and we didn't launch any attacks. We were caught in a situation in which we were broken up into smaller groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your answers. Mr. Bos, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, everyone in the courtroom and outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. We'll have to have your exhibit binder. Maybe the usher can give you the exhibit binder. There's one topic that I still want to discuss with you this morning, and that's the events around mid-April 1993, which you already received some questions from the Presiding Judge. Could I ask you to take a look again at P01911, which is the ECMM report that we've seen before. P01911. Now, sir, I'm going to read out to you Chapter 5 of this report, and then I'll ask you some questions about it. So this report is dated the 16th of April, and under number 5, the officer here describes the present situation in the region: "Conflict rages between the villages north of Lake Jablanica with the HVO villages much better equipped, T-34 [sic] tanks and rockets, much better equipped than Muslim communities. The BiH are: A, attempting to seize the strategic military position of Zlatar, just east of Konjic, which the HVO refused to share; B, blocking the Prozor approach to Jablanica along with HVO armour with approach at Slatina, where a heavily-fortified position exists and large blocks of granite have stopped all vehicle movement; C, expelling all HVO units from Jablanica and Konjic ..." Sir, let's just stop there. So the officer here is describing the situation as regards the BiH Army. What would be your comment on this? Would this be an accurate reflection of the situation on the 16th of April, as far as the BiH Army is concerned and what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as these facts are concerned, the ones you read out, as far as I know, we didn't have T-84 [as interpreted] tanks, at least to my knowledge, but the T-84 [as interpreted] is a large piece of armament, so I think I would have seen it. And as for Zlatar, we spoke a lot about taking that strategic feature. It was our communications centre. The Muslims tried to take it at any price, because if you take away a communications centre from a unit, you have 50 per cent defeated it, because they are left without communication then. And the approach toward Jablanica we know very well from previous documents that we dealt with. And with regard to that, there were orders to block approaches not from -- from Prozor, but from other directions, units from other directions that wanted to go to Konjic. HVO units from Jablanica were mentioned yesterday, and I said that our battalion had problems there, and it pulled out of Jablanica under pressure and went to the village of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So, sir, you would agree that this is an accurate reflection of the situation around mid-April 1993, at least as far as the part that I have read out so far?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree, because I said right away that the arguments are not stated correctly. Did we have a tank? No, we didn't, so I cannot agree with what is said here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: My apologies. You did say that you didn't have tanks, but I was referring to what the BiH Army was doing, and I think there you seem to confirm that what is being said here, it was indeed what the BiH Army was doing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not in this context that is put forward here. They had other intentions and not protecting some facilities or things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I did not pay any particular attention to the issue of the T-54 tank, but I was listening to you and then I wondered whether this report we all can see is accurate. If the author of this report speaks about a T-54, there are two possibilities. Now we can see "T-84." It was T-54, T-54 tank, please. So if this tank did exist, the observers must have seen it, and it's rather unbelievable that you should say that you've never seen any in the area. So what conclusion do you draw? Because there are two possibilities; either the report is wrong or you are lying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am saying that there was no T-84 [as interpreted] tank. Whether there were other armoured vehicles, well, there may have been, but here it is said that the ABiH had a self-propelled Howitzer which looks like a tank, and they took it from Konjic toward our Neretvica Brigade, and the Lisin Detachment made the most use of it. It was positioned above the villages that were mentioned. The Lisin Brigade is a unit of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's continue reading under Chapter 5, and I'll just read it out: "The HVO are attacking the Slatina position with artillery from Ustirama; B, attacking Ostrozac positions, including the obvious refugee centre, with artillery and tank fire from Kostajnica; C, attacking the villages of Here and Scipe north-east of Prozor with artillery from south of Lake Ramsko; D, attacking the units in the Dreznica Valley running west of the Neretva Valley (between Mostar and Jablanica), with tanks and artillery from the south and west; E, shelling Jablanica from Kostajnica and Doljani (west of Jablanica)." So, sir, let me ask you the same question. What do you have to comment about the facts that are being stated here by the ECMM officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to comment this. These EC Monitors may have copied a report of the ABiH where statements are made in an arbitrary fashion, because it is impossible to do some of the things mentioned here; namely, shell Jablanica from Kostajnica over Boksevica. That's utterly impossible. And I don't know what else to say about this report. This is obviously copied from another source, and it's in line with the scenario of the ABiH, which sent the reports to the media and to the UNPROFOR and everybody else around. Yesterday, when you interrupted me, I wanted to speak my mind about some things -- about some events in the Konjic municipality. There were some organised groups. I don't know whether they were part of the civilian or the military structures. At the time, they wore uniforms, but they were tasked to launch a media campaign and to disseminate lies in order to create hatred between the Croats and the Muslims in the area. I wanted to say that yesterday, but you interrupted me, so I thought we might continue today. There were several such groups, and those groups were active not only at Konjic, but in all areas we are discussing now. These groups had the task to work not only on these media plans and information campaigns, they also had the task to buy armaments and communications equipment from the HVO --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you, because you're not responding to my question anymore. What I asked you to say is whether you agreed with the facts that have been described here in this report, and now you're all the way off my question. So please stick to answering my question as to whether you agree with what's being described here as the situation on the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I've been saying, that I don't agree with this report because this report was drafted by such a group as these I mention now. They sent their reports to UNPROFOR, and all the media in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Fine, you don't agree with it. That's enough. Let's have a look at another document, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Since the Prosecutor is about to move on to another document, I have a question on this one. The Prosecutor asked you to confirm that the ABiH had - this is point 5 - carried out the actions as described in this document, and as part of this action, there was Zlatar. You told us that Zlatar was a communication centre. I was listening to you, and I now try to see the Prosecutor's question in their overall case, which is that on the 16th of April, the HVO carried out a large-scale operation against the ABiH, and not the other way around. If the Prosecution's case is right, at that time the ABiH was attacked from all sides in quite a number of locations. But when you are under attack from everywhere, all around, do you counter-attack by taking a communication centre like the one in Zlatar, whilst there may be more relevant objectives when you carry out defensive actions? In military terms, does that make sense? Does it make sense that a party that is attacked is going to defend itself by taking a communication centre? Is that logical, in military terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 14th of April, I believe we said, and corroborated that with documents, that the ABiH attacked the HVO. From no document can it be seen that the HVO attacked the ABiH. Therefore, there was no reason for the ABiH to take the Zlatar facility; only if it was their intention to launch offensive actions which would involve the neutralisation of the communications centre and the neutralisation of the enemy military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're not quite answering my question. I'm going to rephrase it. Let us imagine that you, the HVO, are being attacked by the ABiH. Just a hypothesis. So you're being attacked. And if you are being attacked, you're going to defend yourself. In doing so, are you going to attack the communications centre, the enemy's communications centre? This is what I'm trying to find out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every army, when it attacks any other army, of course a communications centre is a high pay-off target, so logically, taking the communication centre was a priority for the ABiH in this case because it's a core component of a military structure, because without a communication centre, there can be no co-ordination between their units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you don't understand my question. I'm going to repeat it. My starting point is that you are the HVO and you're being attacked. I even imagine that you are the brigade commander, and you're being told that there is an all-out attack by the ABiH. You, as an HVO commander, are you going to tell your men, who are being attacked, that they have to counter-attack by taking the attacker's communication centre? This is a technical question, you see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I answered your question. I said that if we had attacked, I would also have ordered to take the communication centre. I believe I provided that answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I believe the witness didn't understand that the question involved a hypothetical counter-attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Alaburic. Yes, my question is about a counter-attack; not an attack, a counter-attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has obviously been under attack constantly, so probably he has difficulty in adapting to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So he finds it difficult to imagine such a situation. Very well. Please continue, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, could I ask you to take a look at Exhibit P01915, P01915. Now, this is an interim report from Commander Siljeg, inter alia addressed to the HVO Defence Department and the HVO Main Staff, and I want to go into detail into this document. So let's start from the beginning, and then I'll ask you some questions while we're going along. So as I said, it's a report addressed to the Department of Defence of the Main Staff, the Operational Zone Herzegovina, Tomislavgrad: "We are establishing IZM OZ SC Herzegovina at the command of the Rama Brigade. "2. Establish a wire connection with facilities Boksevica, Pisvir, Sovicka Vrata, and with the command of the Mijat Tomic Battalion in the village of Doljani." Let me ask you -- we've discussed Boksevica and we know what Boksevica is, but is it clear that Pisvir and Sovicka Vrata are elevated positions near Sovici/Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear that these are nearby elevations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And we'll continue: "Artillery disposition as follows ..." And then we have a couple of places, and I'm going to ask you if you can identify where those places are: "The village of Dobrosa area," and then, well, I won't read out what -- people can read out what kind of artillery is located there. What I'm interested in is, could you tell me where the Dobrosa area is? I'm not really sure whether you can indicate it on the map, but do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with the area. This is part of the Prozor-Rama Z. Maybe I would be able to locate it, but I can't tell you anything about it. I've never been there. It's a different municipality, different zone, a different brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Which municipality would Dobrosa be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality of Prozor, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And what about the village of Mlusa area, which is the next one under item 3? Is that correct that that's west of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it is also part of Prozor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And then we have the village of Donja Vast. Now, is it correct, sir, that that's east of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you that I'm not very familiar with the Prozor municipality. I've never been in that municipality. Before the war, jobs never took me there, so I'm really not very familiar with Prozor. I can tell you more about Konjic, but as for Prozor, I could search the map and try to locate places, but that would take a lot of time. At this moment, I'm really not prepared to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I wonder whether it makes much sense to ask this witness to locate localities which everyone can find on maps. I suggest that you look at IC693, which is a map of the Prozor area labelled -- actually called "Konjic 1," and you find these localities on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours. I will just continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let me just then say, sir, correct that -- the next is the village of Ustirama. Is it correct that this is about north of Slatina, the location of Ustirama?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ustirama is on the road between Jablanica and Prozor, and it is part of the municipality of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's continue under item number 4 of this report: "Positions towards the villages Here, Kute, Scipe have been secured. The Makljen Pass has been reinforced with one platoon." Can you make any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try and comment. If I am correct in what I think, I believe that the Makljen Pass is a road from Prozor towards Vakuf or, rather, Uskoplje, and I believe that the task of that platoon was to prevent the arrival of any forces from Vakuf. And likewise towards Here, Kute, Scipe, this is where the defence zone was set up, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'll continue to number 5: "Two battle tanks are ready for a show of force and action if needed, and are manoeuvring on axes: The village of Kute, Here, Scipe, and towards the village of Slatina. We do not have enough ammunition for them." Then moving to number 7: "Coordinating with Tuta has been done through the Posusje unit on Sovicka Vrata." Sir, do you know who Tuta was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know who Tuta is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, did Mr. Tuta have anything to do with the operations going on in Sovici and Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had anything to do with the operation. I believe that he was involved in an operation when those villages were being occupied by the BiH Army. He was involved in one action in that stretch around Sovici, but I don't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, it's correct that Sovicka Vrata is an elevated position near Sovici and Doljani; isn't that true? That's what you just confirmed a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, above Sovici, in the direction of Risovac, that's where the Sovicka Vrata is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's read out number 9 of this report: "Requests of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade are unrealistic and make no sense. There is a feeling that they do not know the situation, since the reports are written like children's compositions and newspaper articles and not like military reports. We cannot know what's going on, since we do not have precise reports." Number 10: "According to the submitted requests, we should use up all available ammunition in one day and then do without it." Now, sir, here Commander Siljeg is criticising the reports that are coming from Konjic. Can you comment on what Mr. Siljeg is saying here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say something about the reports from Konjic. Yesterday or the day before, we discussed the situation that our brigade found itself in. The reports were not written by people who were either savvy or were tasked with writing reports, because they'd never been in such situations before. Our brigade, as you can see from this report, was in a very bad condition, without any communication channels, so that the reports that were being sent to our superiors were not sent by commanders or assistant commanders. This was done by platoon commanders. These were not requests. These were cries for help, sir, because if you find yourself in a situation when you have only 20 men, and you're under attack by 200 men and you're defending yourself, those can't be requests but just cries for help, and they cannot be selective. They can go along the lines of, We are asking for assistance. Can you assist us as soon as possible? These were not requests. These were our cries for help. And the supremacy of the enemy was so obvious, and the more powerful they were, the more the commanders cried, and it shows you how much stronger the BiH Army was than the HVO. I can tell you that for each member of the Croatian Defence Council, there were 20 soldiers on the side of the BiH Army. That was the ratio at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, sir, I understand what you're saying, but doesn't it depend really on where in the region you are, because we're talking now here about Konjic and the region where you are, but what about the other regions, you know, in the bordering area of Konjic, Jablanica, Prozor? You're surely not talking about the complete region, Prozor, Jablanica and Konjic, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I am omitting Prozor. I'm talking about the area of responsibility of my brigade. I'm talking about Konjic, the Neretvica Valley and the 1st Battalion there, and I'm talking about the area in the direction of Jablanica. In that part, according to our estimate that we undertook as much as we could, to the extent we were able to make any estimates, one HVO soldier was attacked by 20 soldiers of the BiH Army, so what kind of reports could one expect? Was there anybody able to compose a report, anybody who could get hold of any sort of communication channel? And as I've told you, all the communication channels had been broken by then, so anybody who got hold of such a communication channel cried for help.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, let's just continue reading the report in the last two paragraphs: "There is a wire link to the Herceg Stjepan Command from which we have asked detailed and precise reporting on the situation and precise requests for operations. We continue to work according to plan." Now, sir, would you agree with me that this report from Siljeg confirms the ECMM conclusion that there was an HVO operation in the Prozor-Jablanica-Konjic region and that there was a specific HVO plan to take the region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: An operation was underway in the territories of Konjic and Jablanica, pursuant to a plan by the BH Army that we saw yesterday and the day before yesterday, and that plan showed the exact tasks which had been distributed among the units from Bradina to Jablanica, Aleksin Han, and the axis leading toward Doljani and Sovici and further on towards Prozor.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's have a look at another document, which is P01872.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, before we move on to another document, the Prosecutor omitted reading item 8, and I would like to draw your attention on it. Please take a look at item 8. Two locations are specifically mentioned, the village of Slatina and the village of Sovici. An operation is supposed to occur on Slatina as of 7.00 a.m. and on Sovici as of 9.00 a.m., and what puzzles me is that here we have mention of selected targets. This document from Colonel Siljeg, dates April 16, it's an interim report drawn up at 8.00. It's "202/93." That's the reference number. It would have been interesting to know that -- have a look at item 201, 200, 199. I will do that later, because I have all documents in my office in chronological order, so I'll go check, myself, to see whether documents 201 and 200, you know, also exist. I don't know yet. But if it's an interim report, it means that there must have been a previous report which might have been drafted as of 6.00 a.m. I don't know; maybe. But if that's the case, this document seems to contradict what you're telling us. It would seem that they did prepare to target Slatina and Sovici, and they didn't prepare the targeting on April 16th, but on the 15th, the 14th, or the 13th of April, because there is mention of selected target. It's not targets that have just been selected; they have been selected earlier. So could you tell me how you interpret paragraph 8, in military terms? Does this mean that there was already a plan regarding Slatina and Sovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me remind you of the order issued by the BiH Army from Jablanica, and in that order he sent his units in the axes of Slatina -- let me just see -- Slatina and Sovici. He sent his units in the direction of Slatina and Sovici, and he also sent a sabotage unit which was capable of destroying artillery and all the other armament that was deployed in the area that they assumed that it was Risovac, which means that those units had already taken those positions. And I believe that the order was issued a day or two days before that. I believe that the reports arrived from the field to them, that they had noticed those movements, and that this is what was going on in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I understand you correctly, your explanation is the following: The BH Army attacked, and then the HVO prepared its retaliation and attack, which is why on item 8 Colonel Siljeg planned an operation on Slatina and Sovici. Is that what you told us? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the meaning of my words. The units that had already been entering the sector were discovered, and that's what the gentleman was supposed to do. You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, you might be a bit surprised by my questions, but as Judges we have the following difficulty: We're totally dependent on what information is provided to us by the Prosecution and by the Defence, and we draw our conclusions from the information we've been provided with. In another system, in the civil law system, you know, the judge would have found all orders from the ABiH and all orders from the HVO, and would have compared them and would have seen the light from this comparison, and we would have probably saved an immense amount of time. But I have to put questions to you in order to check many things, with the added difficulty that we do not have the entire documents at hand. If I had been able to do so, I would have looked at Order 201, 200, 199, 198, and I would have also looked at all other orders given by all other operational zones. I would have done the same thing for the 3rd Corps of the BH Army, all the other corps, and I'm sure that we would have found the truth. But we only get part of the information from both sides, which is why we have such difficulties and why I have to put questions to you. Mr. Bos, please pursue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, could I ask you to look at P01872. Now, sir, this is an order from Commander Lasic, dated the 14th of April, 1993, and I'm just going to read out the operative paragraph of this order. It says: "In view of carrying out the combat mission in the Prozor-Jablanica-Konjic area, I order ..." And then what follows is the order. Now, sir, would you agree with me that this language shows that not only Commander Siljeg but also Commander Lasic were involved in this operation, so that both the South-East Operational Zone and the North-West Operational Zone were involved in this combat operation in the Prozor-Konjic-Jablanica area and that both zones were involved in this plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who participated or -- I have not seen this order before. I was not in a position to see it before, because you know where I was at the time. No need to repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's move back one more time to P01911, which is the ECMM report. I'm going to read out to you Chapter number 7, which reads: "The present analysis." It reads: "The HVO wish to secure the Klis region within the framework of or under cover of the Vance-Owen Plan for its military and economic importance. "The HVO are waging a political and diplomatic campaign to seize the region without international intervention or outcry. "At the time of writing, the HVO are making their most serious attempt to isolate Jablanica before seizing it. "Further advances can be expected in the Prozor region, where no ECMM or UNPROFOR presence can intervene at any time. "Any HVO initiative will have to use maximum force to minimise casualties and make maximum progress in as short a time as possible. "The region must be secured before international talks re-start and frustrate any military initiative." Now, sir, it talks about the wish of the HVO to secure the Klis region. Could I ask you to indicate on the map what is the Klis region? Maybe you can turn on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos, I'm looking at the map. Yesterday, the witness circled a number of localities, positioned villages and so on, but I don't think we gave an IC number to this marked map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, sir, we haven't yet, and that's why -- because I intended that he was going to mark a few more things on the map. So we'll give it an IC number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, but don't forget to ask for an IC number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, could you put a circle around the Klis region and mark it with the number C, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A D, rather, because a C has already been used. It should be a D.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is the circle, maybe a bit larger. This would be the region of Klis. It may not be perfectly correct. There may be a place here and there that's outside of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Would you please mark a D in that region, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And if we could now get an IC number for this map, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please, could we have an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The document just marked by the witness shall be given Exhibit IC01129. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct, what the ECMM is saying here, that the HVO were trying to secure the Klis region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: What number was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, you don't have to look at a document, well, unless -- we just read out the ECMM report, and so the ECMM officer is saying that the HVO wanted to secure the Klis region. My question is: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, irrespective of the fact that the UNPROFOR report is being quoted, I believe that my learned friend should clarify the notion "secure," because at that time the area of Klis was under the control of the Croatian authorities, so I'm not really clear as to what my learned friend is aiming at. What is his question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said "secure," Mr. Bos. We would like to know how the witness should interpret the term "secure." What exactly did you mean by "secure," so the witness can answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Whether they wanted to keep control over that region.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As has been already been told, in Klis and the region around it consisted of Croatian or mixed villages, which means that the HVO did not engage in any attacks, nor did it want to attack anything in the area. The situation was as it was. Everybody held their own villages, everybody was in their own villages. Those were local units. The HVO never attempted to cross over to the territory. With Muslims, there was no single case of an HVO soldier -- or a soldier bearing HVO insignia trying to enter a village with a Muslim population. On the other hand, there are documents showing that there were attacks on Buscak on the 13th or on the 14th, which was much before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, another thing that the ECMM report says is that the HVO attempted to isolate Jablanica, and let me just show you Exhibit P01876. Would you have a look at P01876. Now, sir, this is a warning issued by Commander Lasic to Pasalic on the 14th of April, 1993, on ABiH intention to remove the HVO check-point at Radesine, and he's warned not even to think about dislodging the Radesine check-point since it has been located in Croatian Community controlled territory. Now, if you read this order and the tone of this order, would you agree with me that this order doesn't give the impression that the HVO in Konjic is under an attack of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the check-point at Radesine, let me tell you that apart from all efforts to put up joint check-points, which -- and which proved unsuccessful, all along the M-17 highway, let me repeat once again, from Aleksin Han through Jablanica, Ostrozac, Konjic, all the way to Bradina, they were all controlled by the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But we're talking here about Radesine. Was Radesine, on the 14th of April, controlled by the HVO or the ABiH? Just give me an answer to that question, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will, but let me first explain why the Radesine check-point was set up by the HVO, because we didn't have one single check-point on the M-17 road from Jablanica to Bradina. If we wanted to let someone kill us, we could have let them take it. So we had to control the forces because there was intelligence that from Bradina, following the M-17 road, two brigades had passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would appreciate if the Prosecutor would allow the witness to explain, because it goes to this whole notion of tu quoque, the assertions that that's what the Defence is trying to do throughout this case. Now we're hearing an explanation. The Prosecutor is trying to use some ECC report. I'm not sure whether this gentleman actually came in, where he's getting this information. His answer directly impeaches the report, itself. He's giving an explanation why it's there, and it's a contrary explanation as to what the Prosecution is trying to assert; that is, they are trying to isolate Jablanica. And without the explanation, I don't believe that the Trial Chamber can reach a proper decision. So I think the gentleman should be given the opportunity to explain what is there, why it's there, how it got there, and the Trial Chamber can then decide whether that was for the purposes of isolation. And to trust this report of an individual who parachuted into the region and is writing about things that most likely he had no idea about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is now recorded in the transcript, but I wanted to put a follow-up question on Radesine. But I'll let Mr. Bos finish first.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, Witness, what I want to know is - and that's why I asked this question and you only need to answer that particular question - is: If the HVO controlled the Radesine check-point on the 14th of April, is it correct that the ABiH in Jablanica was isolated from Konjic, that no ABiH could move to Jablanica from Konjic as a result of this check-point? Is that correct, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct, and I can explain once more, because if the ABiH controlled everything at Ostrozac and at all other check-points, and according to our intelligence, the M-17 road was used exclusively by the ABiH to move their forces from Jablanica -- that is, from Bradina to Jablanica, and we set up the check-point exclusively for the purpose of controlling traffic and not to return anyone from that check-point, but only to have insight in the movements of the forces of the ABiH. And the gentlemen from the ABiH were bothered by that. We were not bothered by their eight check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you happen to have a follow-up question or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. Witness, we have a document dated 14th of April, signed by Mr. Lasic. It is an order that takes effect at midday, 12.00, on the 14th of April. In this order -- this is document 1872, P1872. In this order, there's mention of various units being positioned, of communications being set up, and also the fact that from a logistical point of view, there should be support set up by the RTP of Medjugorje. What is "RTP"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't found the document. I don't know what "RTP" stands for.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see "RTP-Medjugorje." You don't know what it stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know for sure. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're looking at P1872 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: P1876, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- which is about Radesine. But when reading this document, which is sent to Mr. Pasalic, Mr. Lasic informs him that the Radesine check-point will be controlled by the HVO, but that if ever the ABiH were to try to do anything, action will be taken against Ostrozac, Konjic, Jablanica, and Mostar. This order -- or, rather, this report - it's not an order, this is a report because I see in the English version that it is a report - this report can be interpreted as information given to Pasalic to the effect that from then on, the HVO is going to be in charge of the check-point. The Prosecutor, when he asked you the question, predicated his question on the idea that from this check-point the HVO was trying to isolate Jablanica, was trying to prevent the ABiH from going there. But looking at the map, you notice that this locality, geographically speaking, is between Jablanica and Konjic. It is a hilly region. So in military terms, if you have positions there, you can prevent movement of the ABiH in both directions. And that's the Prosecution case, as I understood it. You answered the Prosecutor's question, in part. You said, No, we were not there in order to control and prevent, but just to check traffic. That's what you said. But when you have a check-point, you can prevent ABiH troops from passing through, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can stop traffic at a check-point, but I have explained why the check-point at Radesine was set up in the first place. I think that the ABiH hasn't mentioned one single instance of a unit of theirs being returned from that check-point, and I have said why the HVO had a reason to set up the Radesine check-point, which means all check-points in the area of the Konjic municipality, from Donja Jablanica to Radisa Han were all controlled by the ABiH, and it's a well-known fact that they were returning HVO members -- turning away. And we set up the check-point to have insight to see where ABiH members were rallying. So the ABiH had eight check-points, and so I guess that we, as the HVO, could -- were entitled to one check-point in a Croatian settlement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A purely technical question. At this check-point, in your view, how was it manned by the HVO; by two people, three people, ten, or by a tank? Who was manning the check-point, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that check-point, there were up to 10 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were up to 10 men. Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's take the Prosecutor's case. He seems to say that from that check-point, the HVO wanted to isolate Jablanica and wanted to prevent the ABiH from getting to Jablanica. Now, is it logical that such a military action or operation would be conducted by only 10 men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've said that the purpose of the check-point was not what the Prosecutor is trying to put forward. We had intelligence reports about forces massing at Donja Jablanica which had come from the direction of Bradina, and we wanted to know whether that was correct or not, so we wanted a check-point to know what kind of units passed by there. And if 10 soldiers were in a position to stop them from passing through, then, yes, we were controlling that, but I don't believe that 10 men could have stopped any ABiH unit from passing through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not aware of the area because I've never been there, but if the Judges had been to this area -- now, if you want to carry out a real military operation, if you want to prevent the enemy from using this road, should you not have put one or two tanks at that check-point? Because given the lay of the land, in that way the ABiH could not have taken the check-point. So you wouldn't have put just 10 men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat once more. It was never our intention to stop anything. The village of Radesine, it is well known, surrendered later to the Spanish Battalion, and there is reliable information that there were about 50 persons there. We had no tanks. These persons were partly civilians, partly soldiers. There was fighting for about 13 days against a much stronger enemy, the ABiH. And once they had run out of ammunition, they had the best intention to surrender to the Spanish Battalion, and that Spanish Battalion handed them over to a sabotage unit called Akrapi, and they took them to Celebici, where they were mistreated, beaten. And one man succumbed to his injuries that were inflicted upon him when they beat him. A few days ago, a Konjic court convicted the perpetrator of that act who beat that man to death. So from the overall strength of units in that area, it was clear that it was not a strong unit that could have prevented the much stronger units of the ABiH from moving down that road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, wasn't the root of the problem of the operations on the 15th of April as follows: The HVO had a plan to take over the Konjic and Jablanica area, an area which is a Muslim-dominated majority area. They tried to attack the area, and it turns out that the ABiH resistance is much stronger and bigger than expected. Is that not what we're talking about here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Let me repeat once more. In the area of the Konjic municipality, the HVO never intended to conduct offensive actions, which can be seen from the documents shown in this courtroom. The ABiH had offensive actions in the direction of Konjic, through Klis and Boksevica, and other units from Jablanica were tasked with taking the area toward Prozor, Risovac, and Boksevica, so we are again speaking about offensive actions of [Realtime transcript read in error "against"] the HVO, but there was never such a thing. And a short while ago, I enumerated to you and showed you how -- in what position the HVO was on the 14th and 16th of April, that these units had been broken up, they had no communication among themselves, they had no communication centre, and I told you what the purpose was of the ABiH attack against the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a correction of the transcript. Line 10 of the current page, the witness said, speaking about the HVO offensive as something that we cannot speak about. So speaking about an HVO offensive, there was never such a thing, and what is stated in the transcript, "offensive actions against the HVO." So the word "against" is something the witness has not uttered. I believe that once that word "against" is omitted, we will get a faithful rendering of the witness's words.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions. I have concluded my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last thing about the Radesine check-point. Do you know the place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Regarding this area or place, is there not a river along it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Jablanica Lake is beneath Radesine, and there is also a railroad line beneath the road, and some 10 metres lower there's the lake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there's the Jablanica Lake. To your knowledge, did the ABiH have boats that made it possible for the ABiH to move along the lake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they didn't have boats, but they passed through the road because we never prevented them from doing so. It was just a check-point which wasn't meant to prevent traffic. There were no barriers of any kind. There was merely a check-point, the purpose of which was to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm just trying to ascertain the Prosecutor's case through my questions. I'm asking you whether it was possible to use the lake to move using boats. This is what I'm trying to find out, and you can tell me whether the ABiH had boats or whether they didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they didn't have any boats, but they were able to use the railroad line, which was open and nobody blocked it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regardless of the railway line, sir, apart from the road, there may have been paths, making it possible for infantrymen from the ABiH to bypass your check-point without any problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And using such paths, would have found themselves under HVO fire, or could they have just gone on without any problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in a position to walk from Celebici and Idbar, bypassing Radesine by descending to Seljani, and from Seljani to Ribici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you tell us that it would not have been easy to go through without problems?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They could have passed without any problems taking the route that I described. It's a foot-path.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because, you see, I wanted to know whether the ABiH soldiers, the infantry soldiers, using those paths, were under the risk of HVO fire or whether they did not run the risk of being seen and, therefore, being fired on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they wouldn't have been exposed to HVO fire because Radesine is a small village, and it's a Croatian village, Croatian-populated village, and they were only defending themselves. And the route that I described is on the other side of the mountain. Celebici-Idbar-Seljani-Ribici, that would have been an easy path to take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The time has come to have a break, and we'll then have the redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Before I forget, I would like to read an oral decision on time allotment for next week. As you know, Witness Filip Filipovic is about to testify next week, and early into next week also. The Trial Chamber has decided that for the Petkovic Defence, the cross-examination and possible redirect will have four hours, the other Defences for cross-examination will have two hours altogether, and the Prosecution will have four hours for his own cross-examination. Ms. Alaburic, you have the floor for the redirect, and the time you take for this will be deducted from your overall time. The Trial Chamber had given you three hours. You've used up all three hours. Now all time spent on the redirect will be deducted from your total time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to thank you. I would like to remind you that during the cross-examination, some new topics were tackled, not having been tackled in the examination-in-chief. I'm going to try and bring this to a swift end.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good morning. Let's start with the questions about the control or check-point in Radesine. You said that that was a check-point and not a point where people were stopped; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Following up on Judge Antonetti's questions, I'm going to have a similar question. If M-17 road was used by a battalion of the BH Army about 300 men strong, and if they wanted to pass along that road, irrespective of the HVO check-point, was there any possibility for those troops to be stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no such possibility. As I've already said, there were about 10 soldiers at the check-point, and if they were faced with 300 troops coming on, of course, they could not have been stopped.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You said that the BiH Army soon gained control over the village of Radesine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you documents dated 14 April 1993. Just a moment. Listen to me. Don't look for anything. He tried to demonstrate to you that the HVO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Alaburic. Bearing in mind the quest for precision that we've heard from Mr. Praljak yesterday, "soon" seems to me a very vague term. What do you mean, "soon," "the ABiH soon gained control"? Does that mean the next day, or the next week, or the next month?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have already seen some documents to that effect, so I did not think that I had to be that precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Maybe the witness can tell us when it was that Radesine fell.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 13 days after the beginning of the aggression against the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: 26th or 27th of April, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Year?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. The Prosecutor showed you documents dated 14 April. I'm going to remind you of a document that we analysed together during the examination-in-chief, and the document speaks about the situation as it was the day before, on the 13th of April. The document is in my binder, towards the end, in the last part speaking about the April events, and the documents follow a chronological sequence. Your Honours, if you want to look at the document yourself, the number is P1874, and the instruction for the witness is just to listen to my question. P1874, P1874. Very well. This is a summary report for the 13th of April. Let's see what happened on the eve of the day when this document was issued or, rather, when the documents that the Prosecutor showed you were issued. It says that on that day, the Croatian village of Buscak was attacked. Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It is also stated herein that the BiH Army had tried to cross the lake from Ostrozac and to take Falanovo Hill. Further on, it says that Buturovic Polje had been shelled. At the moment when the report was being written, Kostajnica is under shelling. Actions were launched in Konjic, which was encircled, as well as Jablanica. And the last sentence reads: "The actions are being stepped up." According to what you know, Witness, was that the situation on the 13th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it was like.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The following report from Konjic, in the same document, states: "The village of Buscak is about to fall. There are a lot of wounded and captured. Urgently act pursuant to our previous request that was sent to Prozor. A lot of reinforcement came from the direction of Jablanica and is moving towards Mrakovo and Zuglici, with an intention to take Boksevica. Buscak has fallen." According to what you know, Witness, was that the situation on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the situation on that day. Buscak fell on that day, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the same document, the third report from Konjic says that the BH Army is opening mortar fire on Ljesovina, Buturovic Polje, and Kostajnica. It says as well that the forces have infiltrated Mrakovo and Djukovica [phoen], although they are still passive, from Orlovac, Ljesovina is being pounded by laser [as interpreted]. An ultimatum was given to Radesine to surrender their weapons before 1300 hours, and Konjic are threatened by forces from Bosnia. And the final conclusion is this is an all-out attack on the entire zone of Jablanica and Konjic. Witness, is this a truthful report or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a truthful report, and this was said already a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has just shown you a document, P187 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this is a question that I will probably put to General Petkovic, but I think I'm also going to ask you about it. We have seen this document, and during the redirect we're seeing it again. This is a report -- a joint report from different operational zones; North-West, Central Bosnia, and South-East. When looking at this document, I am struck by the fact that it seems that things are very quiet on the Central Bosnia front. Well, it's more or less quiet. But in your own area, very serious events are happening, and a great number of events. So when reading this document, according to you, do you think the Main Staff, the central military authority, noting that the situation was such on the south-east front, shouldn't they have sent reinforcement to Konjic, given that the events that were unfolding there? You were there, and did you feel that troops came to your rescue or that you were left alone to deal with the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as we are concerned, the BH Army in our zone, the zone where my brigade was deployed, carried out an aggression against our unit, which could be seen from the previous documents. And then if we remind ourselves of the documents that we also analysed, and one of them was an order by the commander of the Neretva in Jablanica, who says that the BiH Army and the leaders had foreseen that we would seek assistance from operational zones in case of attack, and we did that; however, they had already foreseen that, and the Neretva Brigade commander from Jablanica issued an order and they prevented the arrival of any assistance to us by any unit of the HVO from any part, either from Mostar or Posusje or from Prozor. That means that they prevented access to the units that were supposed to come to our assistance in Aleksin Han, Sovicka Vrata, and the Prozor axis. This means that we were left to our own devices to cope with a much more powerful enemy, and I told you several times what the ratio was between the two of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You said that you were not provided with any reinforcements, but according to you, it's because the BH Army acted in such a way that the troops never were able to come to your rescue. That might be the truth, but there could be another version. And here I'm assuming, but let's assume that for some time the HVO intended to prepare a plan to attack Central Bosnia. Everything was ready, and suddenly the HVO discovers that there is a BH Army attack around Konjic. But since they prepared, they planned their attack for Central Bosnia, they're not budging and they letting you to your own devices, so that on D-Day, i.e., April 16, they can launch their attack starting at Ahmici, Vitez, and so on. Do you believe this version to be plausible or ludicrous?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was not privy to the plan in Central Bosnia. I was not aware of any movements of the HVO in Central Bosnia. I didn't know of any plans, attack plans. I don't know if there were any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you were not privy of anything. Fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, now please rely on the documents that will start appearing on the screen. There's no need for you to go through the bindings. P17886 [as interpreted], 1876, P1876. This is a short report by Miljenko Lasic, sent to Arif Pasalic, with regard to the check-point in Radesine. Very soon you will see it on the screen. My learned friend Mr. Bos told you earlier today, on page 24 of today's record, that the tone of this order reveals that the HVO was preparing an offensive against the BiH Army in the territory of Konjic. Witness, could you please tell me whether Miljenko Lasic, in this document, responds to a threat issued by the BH Army or, rather, whether does he threaten the BH Army? Which is the case here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Mr. Miljenko Lasic's response to BiH Army threats. It is not him threatening anybody. He is, on the contrary, responding to a threat. He says if there is a forcible removal, which means --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Look at the introduction. It says that the BiH Army threatens to remove the HVO check-point in Radesine by force. Does this document contain a threat that the HVO will forcibly remove BiH Army check-points in the same region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. A reference here is exclusively to the check-point in Radesine. Nobody in the HVO threatened anybody else with regard to any check-points. The threat came at the expense of the HVO, against the HVO, and it would be carried through if they did not remove their check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: How do you understand this report? Is this information, on the part of the HVO to the BiH Army, that they intended to defend their check-point, or do they express any offensive intentions with regard to the BiH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just information from the HVO to the BiH Army that they will defend their check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document, P1872, P1872. This is another document issued by Miljenko Lasic. It is an order dated 14 April 1993. We have it on the screen, Witness. Witness, tell me, based on this order, can we say that certain units of the HVO are moving towards certain localities or whether the order has a different effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order orders troops to go to the positions from which they will be able to extend help, if a request for help is sent. This is the 14th, and on the 13th we already asked for assistance from the operations zone, which means that this is an order preparing grounds for extending future help to somebody in a certain sector; in other words, to help us in our sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the localities where troops should have been deployed. A reference is made to Sovicka Vrata, and another reference is made to the direction of movement, Citluk, Ljubuski, Posusje, Rakitno, and Risovac. And then under 8 it says: "Contact shall be established upon arrival in the Risovac area ..." Witness, on the examination-in-chief, did we already encounter the localities of Sovicka Vrata and Risovac? If you remember, could you please give us the context?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did mention the Risovac axis. That was the axis from which the assistance could have come to our brigade from Posusje. That was one of the axes along which we could have expected help in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, I'm going to say what was the order that we analysed. It was an order by Enes Kovacevic, commander of the BH Army, dated 14 April, and the document number is 2D246 [Realtime transcript read in error "426"]. Witness, you will probably remember, but if you don't, we will look at the document. Did this document set out that the BiH Army would take certain positions precisely at the localities around Sovicka Vrata and Risovac in order to prevent the arrival of the HVO assistance in the territory of Jablanica and Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't have to read, but I can tell you that one BiH company was sent in the direction of Sovici and Doljani and that a sabotage unit was sent directly to Sovicka Vrata. In keeping with their assumption, that was the only platoon from which fire could have been opened, they did not have to go any further in depth. That was the only elevation where artillery could be positioned. They sent their sabotage unit to intervene in case artillery had been positioned or there were attempts to position artillery on that elevation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let me first correct the number of this document. In line 8, the document number is 2D246. Now it is correct. Let's look at the following document - it will be on the screen - P1915, 1915. That's correct. This is an interim report by the commander of the OZ, Zeljko Siljeg. You have it on the screen. Maybe we can reduce the size to display the entire page. Now I'm going to draw your attention to two elements in this report. Under bullet point 9, the requests and reports from the Herceg Stjepan Brigade are qualified. You've already spoken about that in great length. And then under 12, it says that: "Wire connection has been established with the command of the Herceg Stjepan, and we request detailed and precise information about the situation from them, and we also request a precise request for action." My question to you is this: You have read the entire information, because my learned friend Mr. Bos also showed it to you. Would you conclude, based on this report, that the operations zone of Mr. Siljeg had some independent offensive plans for action against Jablanica or were they, rather, waiting for precise requests from the Konjic Brigade in order to launch their actions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this report, I can see -- everybody can see that Zeljko Siljeg did not have any offensive intentions. He was waiting for reports from our brigade. He did not want to act pursuant to the cries for help by lower-ranking officers. Mr. Zeljko Siljeg established wire communication instead with our communications centre, I suppose, in order to be able to tell exactly and act precisely on the most critical parts. This means that no offensive activities were being prepared. Things would have started moving in case the Herceg Stjepan Brigade sent precise instructions for assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Witness, I would like you to explain to me what, then, the number 8 of this order means, where we read: "Beginning of today's operation on selected targets next to the village of Slatina, seven hours, and on the village of Sovici, nine hours." I do not see that this means waiting for some request, but maybe you can explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have just explained things with regard to bullet point 8 in connection of Sovici and Slatina, if I'm not mistaken. At 7.00, Sovici, Slatina -- if you remember the order that we saw here, that one company of the Neretva Brigade from Jablanica should be sent to the sector that we're dealing with, which is the sector of Slatina and Sovici, and I believe that even one day prior to that they entered that part with their units and positioned their artillery, I suppose, and deployed troops, I suppose. And most probably troops noticed those movements and they requested from Mr. Siljeg to help them in that part. And that's why he answers and says, We'll do it tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I note that two times you say "I suppose" in this answer, so you're not quite sure. It's something that you think, rather than something that you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not what I think. I said that everybody knows that, and I was answering the same question coming from the Presiding Judge. I was not there to be able to tell you exactly, This is this. However, in view of the document that we looked at and by which the commander of the Neretva Brigade from Jablanica sent his units into those areas, that means that those units of the BiH Army were already on the ground and actually they were carrying out tasks that they had been given, which means that they were preparing themselves for assault or had already launched an assault. And it is only logical that our members, members of our 3rd Battalion, Mijo Tomic, who were deployed in the area, requested assistance in artillery or in any other form from Zeljko Siljeg, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, we have just seen a summary report for the 13th of April. This is P1874. In that document, there is a reference to the 13th of April, and it says that from the area of the Konjic and Jablanica region, requests were sent for assistance. I've found the exact sentence. It says: "Urgently act upon our previous requests that we sent to Prozor," in other words, to the OZ of Zeljko Siljeg. Is it true, Witness, that already on the 13th of April, a request was sent to Zeljko Siljeg's OZ that your brigade, or some elements thereof, sent appeals and requests for assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to the document that we saw by Zeljko Siljeg, P1915, 1915. In item 12, Zeljko Siljeg says that he expects precise requests for action. Why does he stress "precise requests"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wants precise requests for operation to be able to open fire at military targets that threaten the units in our area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, as a soldier, tell us, if Zeljko Siljeg had been preparing for offensive actions, would you know which targets he was planning to attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If he had wanted to launch offensive actions, in the plan for these actions the targets would have been identified which were to be attacked or destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems to me that my question doesn't make sense the way it was interpreted. I will repeat. My question was: If Zeljko Siljeg had planned offensive actions, would he, that is, Zeljko Siljeg, know which targets he wants to attack? The question was interpreted as if I had asked the witness whether the witness would have known, but the witness gave a correct answer because he listened to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at document P1911 now, please, 1911. This is the report by the European Commission Monitors. You have answered many questions about that. I will go into paragraph 5 of that report, and I will not elicit summary assessments of what is correct and what is wrong. But let us see whether there are correct elements in there, after all. We will not deal with the value judgements of the monitors, because they are not relevant for the proceedings. It is said here that the ABiH are attempting to seize Zlatar. Tell me, is this a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that the ABiH are blocking the Prozor approach to Jablanica and setting up heavy granite blocks as obstacles. Do you have any knowledge about blocking the approach to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that the ABiH were blocking? I didn't understand well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Sub-item B reads that the ABiH are blocking the approach to Jablanica from Prozor, and it goes on to say that they are positioning granite blocks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, because we know from the document issued by the commander of the Neretva Brigade from Jablanica that a company was sent to that area, and it was tasked to block the road from Prozor to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In item 5(c), it says that the ABiH wants to expel all HVO units from Jablanica and Konjic. As far as you know about the situation on the ground, is that a correct statement or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The report continues to mention the activities of the HVO. Please listen carefully. It is said the HVO are attacking the Slatina position with artillery. They are attacking the positions at Ostrozac. They are attacking the villages of Here and Scipe. They are attacking the units in the Dreznica Valley. I'll ask you about these localities now. If we try to link these places to the order issued by Enes Kovacevic on the 14th of April, which is document 2D246, if you remember, are those localities where the ABiH had its positions in order to prevent the arrival of HVO units to help the Konjic HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the very positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Witness, I'm going to ask you a few short questions now about UN documents and a testimony in the Blaskic case. The report of the Secretary-General of the UN, document P1391. You just listen. 1391, dated February 2, 1993. In item 1, it says, paragraph 1, the participants included the leaders from the three sides in Bosnia-Herzegovina, including President Alija Izetbegovic, Radovan Karadzic, and Mate Boban. In item 8, these three persons are mentioned again, and it is stated that Mate Boban -- we're talking about the Vance-Owen Plan. Mate Boban had signed the agreement setting out the constitutional principles, the provincial map, and the agreement on military issues; furthermore, that President Izetbegovic had accepted the constitutional principles and the military agreement, but did not accept the map. Mr. Karadzic had not yet answered. Paragraph 9 again mentions three sides in Bosnia. According to your information, Witness, were there three parties -- conflicted parties, in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time; namely, the Muslim side, the Serbian side, and the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, was Radovan Karadzic the leader of the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, was Mate Boban the leader of the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, was Alija Izetbegovic the leader of the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Alaburic, I cannot help wondering about these questions. These are facts that are before us since three and a half years. Why do we need a witness to confirm again? I think it's a sheer loss of time. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I disagree, because in this courtroom Alija Izetbegovic is constantly called the president of a country supposed to -- that fought in the interests of all citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the ABiH is consequently being presented as the only legitimate military force in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: We have heard a lot of argument to the contrary also.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Your Honour, let me just say that every now and then a question is asked whether or not the HVO was legal, or whether it was a paramilitary formation, or I don't know what kind of military force, and I believe that this must be clarified, and it will also be significant later. I just have one question left for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, having defined the three sides this way, can you tell us who, in your opinion, took care, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, simultaneously of all three peoples and every citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there was no such person or body. Everybody took care of their own people.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I will now remind you of a document the Prosecutor showed you, and that is P11086, 11086. It's a report by Zarko Keza, dated December 7, 1992, which says that some ABiH commanders said that the Croats would get only 25 per cent of managerial positions in the army. At that moment in late 1992, that was roughly the share of Croatian population in the overall population of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the 1990 census, Konjic -- in Konjic, there were 26 -- or, rather, precisely 27 per cent of Croatian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness, as a Croat at Konjic at the time, were you or any of your friends afraid of the situation that you Croats would have such a share in the authorities as the Muslims were inclined to cede you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were afraid, because if the Croats accounted for 27 per cent of the population, and if we say that in 1992 the Serbian people left the municipality of Konjic, and a real percentage, according to the census, was being reduced, so that we were no longer 27 per cent; we accounted for a larger share because the Serbs were no longer there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you provide me a brief answer to the question whether you Croats were afraid that you would have only those rights that the Muslims, who were the majority population, were willing to give you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my redirect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, on behalf of the Trial Chamber I want to thank you for testifying as a Petkovic Defence witness. I wish you all the best for your return back home, and I'm going to ask the usher to kindly escort you out of the courtroom. It may be the last thing he's going to do in this courtroom. Ms. Alaburic, with regard to next week, you're going to meet up with the witness, you're going to proof him, and he should be availability for the Trial Chamber on Monday afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, next week we are moving north to Central Bosnia, and we will also deal with some other issues. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So failing other questions by the parties, I want to thank everybody. We shall reconvene on Monday, but do prepare for the next testimony. I wish you a very good weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 30th day of November, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: [The accused Coric and Pusic not present]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.35 a.m.,
